newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called steady after Friday gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called steady after Friday gains.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open steady Monday following Friday's gains on news of maintenance cuts next week on the main transmission lines linking the Northwest to southern California.

In over-the-counter business, September Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $30.00-30.40 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Friday's settlement at $30.33, and September California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $22.75-23.00 versus Friday's close at $22.90.
During early cash activity, firm peak power prices at PV were quoted at $29.00-29.50 a MWh and at COB $18.00-21.00.
The 3,800 megawatt (MW) AC segment of the Pacific Intertie was scheduled at 2,950 MW between 0800-1600 PDT Monday to Friday, while the DC line will be limited to 2,360 over the same period.
A high pressure ridge building in the West is expected to heat the region's temperatures three to seven degrees F above normal through Friday, meteorologists said.

In its latest six to 10 day forecast, Weather Services Corp said temperature would average below normal along the coastal region, near normal further inland and above normal in the eastern part of the Southwest.
Despite outlook of rising temperature and slightly less cheap Northwest hydropower to the Southwest this week, analysts said the September contracts will likely trade within their recent ranges.
"It's just very quiet this morning," a New York futures broker said.
Most baseload units in the West were said to be operating normally early Monday.
The 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Palo Verde generating complex in Arizona continued to coast down toward its refueling outage in September.
The unit, in Wintersburg, Ariz., was operating at 81 percent power early Monday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
